Title: May 21, 2026 City of Boulder City Council Meeting (Regular Meeting)
Overview: The May 21, 2026 regular meeting centered on public comment about the San Lazaro mobile home park purchase, Boulder Municipal Airport local control, and lease and service changes at Golden West Manor, with council and staff pledging to coordinate with the county, explore financial support, and return to the airport topic later. Council approved the consent agenda, with Councilmember Wallach voting no on item 3B, and unanimously adopted Ordinance 8750 for the $18.6 million first budget adjustment. Council also agreed to add non-binding language for straw polls and to clarify how study sessions can be used, while no council members called up the 777 Broadway or 990 Arapahoe items.

Topic1.Title: Open Comment: San Lazaro Mobile Home Park Purchase
Topic1.Summary: Multiple San Lazaro residents and a steering committee spoke in Spanish and English through interpretation, describing displacement fears, rising lot rents under private equity ownership, and a $42.5 million purchase offer. Speakers asked the city to help residents buy the park and to raise the issue with Boulder County. Council members and staff responded that the city supports the effort, is coordinating with the county, and is splitting the cost of a new appraisal. Staff said financial support options are being explored.

Topic2.Title: Open Comment: Boulder Municipal Airport and FAA Local Control
Topic2.Summary: Several residents urged council to place a ballot measure before voters on keeping local control of the municipal airport rather than accepting FAA grants that impose long-term obligations. Speakers raised noise, leaded fuel, and enforcement concerns, and cited airports in Santa Monica and Torrance as examples of local control. A speaker also said council's recent study session on the airport relied on incomplete information and asked for a do-over. Staff responded that funding decisions depend on future land use and that CDOT funding limits had been misstated, with the topic to return to council.

Topic3.Title: Open Comment: Golden West Utilities and Lease Changes
Topic3.Summary: Golden West Manor residents, many of them seniors on fixed incomes, said cable, TV, and telephone services will no longer be included in their leases starting September 1, and that parking now costs $50 per month. They also raised elevator reliability problems in the 14-story building. Staff said the Comcast contract is ending, free Wi-Fi will continue with a rent reduction of about $40 to $45, and Boulder Housing Partners will provide support for transitioning residents.

Topic4.Title: Open Comment: Other Public Comments on Wages, Housing, and Civic Issues
Topic4.Summary: Speakers addressed a range of topics including opposition to the tipped minimum wage freeze and support for a vacancy tax, a request for a streamlined city process for tree-protection and lot reviews, and a proposal for Colorado independence. Other speakers raised concerns about federal actions, international conflicts, and the rights of residents. Council members and staff thanked speakers and responded briefly.

Topic5.Title: Consent Agenda Items 3A and 3B
Topic5.Summary: Council approved the consent agenda with a motion and second. Councilmember Wallach voted no on item 3B, an ordinance amending Title 7 height limitations, citing imprecise drafting. Items 3A and 3B passed unanimously otherwise.

Topic6.Title: Call-Up Check-Ins: 777 Broadway Site Review and 990 Arapahoe Landmark
Topic6.Summary: No council members called up the 777 Broadway site review for redevelopment with 63 residential units, or the Landmarks Board decision not to designate 990 Arapahoe Avenue as an individual landmark. Mayor Pro Tem Weiner used the landmark item to suggest reviewing the landmarking process at next year's retreat, citing conflicts with affordable housing and displacement.

Topic7.Title: Public Hearing: First Adjustment to Base Budget (ATB1) and Ordinance 8750
Topic7.Summary: Staff presented ATB1, an $18.6 million budget adjustment including $13.1 million from fund balance, $5.3 million in mid-year grants, and $129,000 in additional revenue. Most fund balance draws are restricted to specific purposes such as radio replacement for public safety, affordable housing projects, and wildfire programs. The public hearing included comments on the budget and a discussion of communications staffing. Council unanimously adopted Ordinance 8750.

Topic8.Title: Matters: Study Session Procedures, Straw Polls, and Reconsideration
Topic8.Summary: City Attorney Teresa Taylor Tate explained that official action occurs only at regular or special meetings, while study sessions provide non-binding direction to staff. Council discussed how straw polls function, what counts as a material change warranting reconsideration, and how consent items and calls-up work. Council agreed to add non-binding language for straw polls and to clarify that study sessions may include information-only items, with staff to provide a summary of look-ahead agenda items.
